brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A broken black tea from Nanchuan in Chongqing, made from Yunnan large-leaf bushes and known for a strong, brisk cup.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: It first appeared in 1975 and was developed for export, with Nanchuan named a production base for quality broken black tea. A batch sold under the Emei label is reported to have won gold at the 25th Geneva international food fair in 1986 and at a Chinese world expo in 1988. It was counted among the five 'golden flowers' of Sichuan tea.
processing: Withered, rolled, cut by rolling and sifting repeatedly, then oxidized and dried. The raw leaf is mostly one bud with two or three leaves, at least half of it one bud with two.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Tight, heavy granules with a dark, glossy color.
taste_profile: Strong, brisk and fresh, with a high, lasting aroma.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
